athanasius-of-alexandria.modern: He became human so that we might be made God.
athanasius-of-alexandria.printed: He was made man that we might be made God.
athanasius-of-alexandria.uncertain: "We might be made God" keeps the passive of the Greek: God does the deifying. "We might become God" is a second reading that loses this.

athanasius-of-alexandria.modern: our blessed Father Athanasius, praised by all.
athanasius-of-alexandria.printed: our blessed and all-celebrated Father Athanasius.
athanasius-of-alexandria.uncertain: "All-celebrated" means praised by everyone. "Highly honoured" is a weaker second reading.

constantine-the-great.modern: the first of the emperors who began to be zealous for the Church
constantine-the-great.printed: the first of the emperors who began to be zealous for the Church.

ephrem-the-syrian.modern: Look, on your behalf I appoint myself to run the shelter.
ephrem-the-syrian.printed: See, on your behalf I appoint myself hospitaller.
ephrem-the-syrian.uncertain: "On your behalf" may mean "as your agent, with your money" or "for your sake". "Hospitaller" means one who runs a house of care for strangers, the poor and the sick, so readings include "shelter" and "guesthouse".

gregory-of-nazianzus.modern: We seemed to have one soul living in two bodies.
gregory-of-nazianzus.printed: We seemed to have one soul, inhabiting two bodies.

gregory-of-nazianzus.modern: Why should I fight over piglets and chickens, and ones that are not my own,
gregory-of-nazianzus.printed: Why should I fight for sucking pigs and fowls, and those not my own,

gregory-of-nazianzus.modern: as if I were fighting for souls and church canons?
gregory-of-nazianzus.printed: as though for souls and canons?
gregory-of-nazianzus.uncertain: "Canons" may mean church rules or a bishop's canonical rights of jurisdiction, which were at stake in the quarrel. Both readings are kept.

gregory-of-nazianzus.modern: equally far from the merging of Sabellius and from the division of Arius,
gregory-of-nazianzus.printed: equally far from the confusion of Sabellius and from the division of Arius,
gregory-of-nazianzus.uncertain: "Confusion" here means fusing Father, Son and Spirit into one, not bewilderment. "Division" means splitting God into unequal parts.

gregory-of-nyssa.printed: received the legacy of Eunomius' controversy.
gregory-of-nyssa.uncertain: "Eunomius' controversy" means the dispute against Eunomius that Basil left unfinished. This is read from the context. The English alone could mean a dispute that belonged to Eunomius.

gregory-of-nyssa.modern: of the same rank as the Father and the Son.
gregory-of-nyssa.printed: of the same rank as the Father and the Son.

john-chrysostom.modern: Glory to God for all things.
john-chrysostom.printed: Glory to God for all things.
john-chrysostom.note: The two renderings were made on the same words as printed in npnf109 l.1990-1997, an editor's citation of this saying.

methodius-of-olympus.modern: with the same parts, uninjured and immortal, while sin is utterly and entirely destroyed.
methodius-of-olympus.printed: with the same parts, uninjured and immortal, while sin is utterly and entirely destroyed.
methodius-of-olympus.uncertain: The printed text doubles the emphasis ("utterly and entirely"). One reading keeps the doubling, and the other has the plain "completely destroyed".

origen.modern: Be careful not to change your mind because of us.
origen.printed: Take heed not to change your mind on our account.
